positiveChapeauEvidenceAnalysis.conclusion: with current metadata the layer cannot distinguish a genuinely empty content-bearing chapeau from a substantive lead-in whose semantics are scanner-invisible. The ONE positive proof it possesses is the existing canary #2 predicate isPureClauseIntroducer: every content word is a subordinating connective and the fragment carries no object (no value, digit, reference noun or quotation). That is a positive identification of the whole fragment as a connective, not an absence test.

newChildDescentRule: A parent residue is discharged COVERED_BY_CHILD_DESCENT only when ALL of: (1) every child unit is fully accounted (no UNACCOUNTED_SOURCE span); (2) every child unit carries at least one semantically OWNED span (COVERED_BY_INVENTORY or ACCOUNTED_BY_EXTERNAL_UNIT - artifact 32, unchanged); (3) the residue is the final coordination fragment of the parent and runs up to the children (canary #4, unchanged); (4) the residue is POSITIVELY a bare subordinating connective per isPureClauseIntroducer (canary #2 predicate, reused, not extended). The former test `values.length === 0` is deleted: the scanner participates only as positive evidence inside (4) (a value makes the fragment not bare). Any content-bearing residue stays UNACCOUNTED_SOURCE with a reason naming the owned children and stating that absence of a recognised value is not proof.
